I just finished the game. The negative reviews are way off.

This is a great game. Level design is superb. Very atmopsheric world. 

It is exactly what it looks like - Dark Souls with guns.

You have to persist and be patient and farm and strategize just like you'd do any other Souls game.

I assume the people who wrote negative reviews quit the first time the game got a little challenging.

This game takes work, endurance, patience, and persistence. Do that, and you'll miss it when it's over.

This may sound generic, but its Dark Souls with guns. And think Dark Souls Prepare to Die edition. The controls are just as likely to kill you as the enemy is. (there is no jumping, but you seem to be able to roll over small gaps, gives me a heart attack every time.) So if a little rage is your style give this one a closer look, just at the time of this typing (2/20) keep shadows down to low, they seem to be a bit of a performance hog right now.
its fun im liking what they did to soul-like. still you can tell its an AA video game but that's no reason to right it off. Sold 5/10

Excellent game. Really interesting how they blended Souls-like gameplay into a shooter, with interweaving paths that encourage exploration, character build variety, and some incredible and challenging boss battles.  I would recommend this to any fan of the Souls series. This is a game made by a relatively small team, and although there were VERY minor graphical hiccups, glitches, and some pacing issues, I had a great experience with it. The aesthetic is a little bland for my taste (cybernetic Norse mythology), but the play and game-feel is top notch.  I hope there's a sequel that will expand upon the ideas here; but as it is, I think it's a must play. It's the most a game has kept me coming back for more in a long time.

I got this as a gift, and it's really great. The start was rough due to lack of weapon choices, and you have no idea what stats you'll need. You do get a respec flask though, so it's not like you're doomed if you mess up your build due to early ignorance.

Some strategy tips: 

[list]
    [*] Put a lot of points into Finesse and Perception - these should be your highest stats. Keep Expertise and Insight about equal to one another and they should be the second highest. This will enable the use of high level sniper rifles that are easily the best weapons in the game. You will 1HKO most enemies aside from bosses, and bosses will go down quickly.

    [*] Couple the rifle with the aspect that gives you one spare ammo for your equipped gun when you kill an enemy. When you 1HKO nearly everything you will never run out of sniper rifle ammo, and if you do you will have a lot of ammo packs because you rarely use them.

    [*] Patience, like all souls-like games, is key. Use that sniper rifle to kill enemies by shooting them in the back before they see you. This will sometimes mean waiting for them to turn around. It's important to 1HKO your enemies to ensure you don't use ammo.
    
    [*] If you can't hit their back, shoot their head. It's not as good, but it's still a weak spot. Most unarmored enemies will die to a sniper rifle headshot if you build properly. Eventually most unarmored enemies will die to a bodyshot.
[list]

This had the potential to be Brilliant, but now i only look at it as average at best now, major clipping issues that cause you to lose large amounts of Bits, movement and aiming is very rigid and clanky (like driving a tank) this is one of those games that make you think that they should have fired just one person when they made this game.
On the flip side, it's got a lot of good feeling abd good ideas with a gun like souls, yes Dark Souls with guns. if only it had the actual polish and fine tuning of Dark souls

I really like this game but I can understand why people may have some problems with it.  I thought it was a bold move and, for the most part, the game works well.  There are some frustrating aspects but overall I would rate it highly for trying something so different.

This game gave me back the souls-feeling.

To be fair, the start was rough. It took a while to get familiar with the mechanics.
As with dark souls, I restarted the game after I beat the second boss, and with the new 
character I had a much easier time knowing what to expect (especially how stats work, and what weapons require to be used).

I recommend every souls-fan to give this a try - and remember how convoluted dark souls felt at first ;-) It takes time. Thats not a bad thing.
